frankenfield2005.journal: Journal of the American Dietetic Association

cunningham1991.title: Body composition as a determinant of energy expenditure: a synthetic review and a proposed general prediction equation
cunningham1991.journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition

refalo2023.title: Influence of Resistance Training Proximity-to-Failure on Skeletal Muscle Hypertrophy: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis

zourdos2016.title: Novel Resistance Training–Specific Rating of Perceived Exertion Scale Measuring Repetitions in Reserve
zourdos2016.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research

nuckols.title: The Evidence is Lacking for “Effective Reps”
nuckols.label: Nuckols, Stronger By Science

fao2004.title: Human energy requirements: report of a joint expert consultation, Rome, 17–24 October 2001
fao2004.journal: FAO Food and Nutrition Technical Report Series 1, table 5.3
fao2004.label: FAO/WHO/UNU 2004

helms-2014-protein.title: A Systematic Review of Dietary Protein During Caloric Restriction in Resistance Trained Lean Athletes: A Case for Higher Intakes
helms-2014-protein.journal: International Journal of Sport Nutrition and Exercise Metabolism
helms-2014-protein.support: Six studies; protein needs for energy-restricted resistance-trained athletes are likely 2.3-3.1 g/kg of FFM scaled upwards with severity of caloric restriction and leanness.

hall-2007.title: What is the required energy deficit per unit weight loss?
hall-2007.support: The rule of thumb approximately matches the predicted energy density of lost weight in obese subjects with an initial body fat above 30 kg but overestimates the cumulative energy deficit required per unit weight loss for people with lower initial body fat.

jager-2017.title: International Society of Sports Nutrition Position Stand: protein and exercise
jager-2017.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
jager-2017.support: Higher protein intakes (2.3-3.1 g/kg/d) may be needed to maximize the retention of lean body mass in resistance-trained subjects during hypocaloric periods.

lieberman-2018.title: Menstrual Disruption with Exercise Is Not Linked to an Energy Availability Threshold
lieberman-2018.support: Thirty-five sedentary, ovulatory women age 18 to 24 yr completed a diet and exercise intervention over three menstrual cycles. The likelihood of a MD decreased by 9% for each unit increase in EA (odds ratio, 0.91; 95% confidence interval, 0.84-0.98). No specific value of EA emerged as a threshold below which MD were induced.

harvie-2011.title: The effects of intermittent or continuous energy restriction on weight loss and metabolic disease risk markers: a randomized trial in young overweight women
harvie-2011.support: 107 overweight or obese premenopausal women over 6 months: about 2,710 kJ a day on 2 days a week lost as much weight as a daily 25% restriction.

trepanowski-2017.title: Effect of Alternate-Day Fasting on Weight Loss, Weight Maintenance, and Cardioprotection Among Metabolically Healthy Obese Adults: A Randomized Clinical Trial
trepanowski-2017.support: Fast days at 25% of energy needs alternating with feast days lost no more weight than a daily 25% restriction over a year, and more people dropped out.

authors: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
nice-2025.title: Overweight and obesity management (NG246): physical activity and diet
nice-2025.label: NICE 2025
nice-2025.support: Low-energy diets (800 to 1,200 kcal a day) and very-low-energy diets (under 800) only within specialist services, for no more than 12 weeks.

helms-2023.title: Effect of Small and Large Energy Surpluses on Strength, Muscle, and Skinfold Thickness in Resistance-Trained Individuals: A Parallel Groups Design
helms-2023.support: 21 trained lifters randomized, 17 completers over 8 weeks; maintenance vs 5% vs 15% energy surplus; faster rates of body mass gain primarily increase rates of fat gain rather than augmenting strength or muscle thickness.

nunes-2022.title: Systematic review and meta‐analysis of protein intake to support muscle mass and function in healthy adults
nunes-2022.journal: Journal of Cachexia, Sarcopenia and Muscle
nunes-2022.support: Increasing daily protein ingestion may enhance gains in LBM in studies enrolling subjects in RE; significant for younger subjects (<65 years old) ingesting >=1.6 g of protein/kg/day.

fao2010.title: Fats and fatty acids in human nutrition: report of an expert consultation
fao2010.label: FAO/WHO 2010
fao2010.support: Minimum to prevent essential fatty acid deficiency: 2.5% of energy as linoleic acid plus 0.5% as alpha-linolenic acid. Minimum total fat for adults 15% of energy; maximum 30-35% for most.

who2003.title: Diet, nutrition and the prevention of chronic diseases: report of a joint WHO/FAO expert consultation
who2003.label: WHO/FAO 2003
who2003.support: Fruits and vegetables and wholegrain foods are likely to provide more than 25 g a day of total dietary fibre; at least 400 g a day of fruits and vegetables.

hodgdon1984m.title: Prediction of percent body fat for U.S. Navy men from body circumferences and height

hodgdon1984f.title: Prediction of percent body fat for U.S. Navy women from body circumferences and height

foulis2023.title: Body composition changes during 8 weeks of military training are not accurately captured by circumference-based assessments
foulis2023.support: Tape-method body fat against DXA in 1,407 Army recruits: standard error of estimate 3.42 points (men) and 4.12 (women) before training, reading about 6 points below DXA on average.
